dimensions.name: Contract & reference mining

evidence.note: Systematic upfront orientation: reads root+all crate Cargo.tomls, all stubs, counts tests, then extracts contract from tests (imports catalog, ObjectMeta/TypeMeta usage, JSON key expectations, resource-type name list) and dispatches sub-agents to catalog the common::resources API — anchor-8-level test-contract extraction breadth.

Per-type derivation of exact serde field names, enum variants (KeyUsage JSON strings), and struct fields from test literals before writing each resource module — genuine test-driven signature/field-name reconstruction, not from memory.

For storage crate, mines watch/key usages and build_key/prefix assertions from tests to reconstruct the storage-key shape and Storage trait surface, then implements — probing the contract rather than guessing.

Before implementing controller-manager, systematically reads every controller test file and uses multiple sub-agents to extract per-controller specs — sustained per-crate contract extraction; dependency-respecting leaf-to-root ordering.

No tool call ever accesses /opt/k8s-reference; all K8s semantics are derived from test fixtures and memory. The reference-mining half of the dimension — explicitly present from anchor 5 upward and emphasized for the hidden conformance suite — is entirely absent.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent performs exemplary, systematic reconstruction of the public API from tests, stubs, and manifests — extracting types, module paths, serde field names, and storage-key shape per crate and probing the dependency graph for leaf-to-root ordering, which matches anchor-8 rigor on the test-contract axis. However, it never once consults the mounted upstream v1.35 reference, coding K8s semantics from memory/fixtures instead of the source of truth; reference cross-checking is required even at anchor 5. This split — strong test-mining, zero reference-mining — lands the observed behavior at a 6: clearly above the crate-local minimum of 5 in breadth, but capped below 8 because half the named dimension (reference mining) is missing.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Leaf-first execution: builds and tests common (259/261) as a milestone, then a TodoWrite (264) transitions to storage, built at 333 — dependency-respecting order with concrete build/test done-checks per crate.
Explicit milestone gating between crates: scheduler run as exit test (1432 area) before a TodoWrite (1029) moves on to controller-manager, sustaining ordered forward motion.

Decomposes the largest crate: pilots the replicaset controller with its own compile+test exit check (1331/1332) BEFORE fanning out ~20 remaining controllers, then a full controller-manager test run (1368) — sub-module sequencing with foundation verified first.
Re-sequences back to the common foundation to add types (autoscaling, secret codec) as higher crates reveal needs — adaptive DAG discovery rather than forcing dependents forward.

kubelet delegated wholesale in one Agent call (not decomposed), then whole-workspace build/test (1486/1491) and test-count reconciliation — final milestone but hardest crates (api-server, kubelet) not internally checkpointed, capping below 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit, dependency-aware leaf-to-root plan with milestones tied to concrete checks (per-crate build then provided-test green), used TodoWrite to track sub-goals across a very long horizon, sequenced sub-modules within the largest crate via a verified pilot-then-fan-out pattern, and re-sequenced to the common foundation as dependencies were discovered — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It stops short of 10 because api-server (a hardest crate) was a reactive compile-fix loop rather than a checkpointed sequence with explicit exit tests, and kubelet was delegated as a single undifferentiated block.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond provided fixtures

evidence.note: After implementing common and storage, builds then runs each crate's provided tests — establishes the per-crate build/test loop (anchor 5).
Sustained 'recompile api-server tests, list errors' iteration driving compile/test errors to zero across dozens of fixes; verification loop maintained across a long horizon.
Runs api-server tests, inspects specific failure details (930/933), re-runs previously failing tests after storage fixes, aggregates pass/fail counts — iterating until provided tests pass.
Builds entire workspace, compiles all workspace tests, runs the full workspace suite, and sums total passed/failed — the workspace-wide run of anchor 5-8.

Counts test attributes, finds in-source test modules, and 'distinguishes real failures from test-name matches' plus checks for hidden failures — demonstrates the counted-vs-non-counted awareness of anchor 8.

Semantic checks (JSON key expectations, storage build_key/prefix asserts) are driven entirely by the provided fixtures — no independent conformance probes; no binary boot or HTTP validation anywhere in the trajectory (anchor-8 end-to-end validation absent).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs the prescribed per-crate and workspace test commands and iterates until provided tests pass (anchor 5), and goes beyond it by carefully distinguishing counted vs non-counted tests in the final accounting (in-source modules, test-name matches, hidden failures — an anchor-8 clause). However it never boots the all-in-one binary or validates end-to-end HTTP/JSON/storage-key semantics against the reference to anticipate the hidden conformance suite, and authors no semantic probes — so it misses the central behaviors of anchors 8 and 10. This lands between 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across 100 binaries

evidence.note: TodoWrite ledger created and updated at every crate milestone across the whole horizon — an explicit, sustained done-vs-remaining picture rather than ad hoc tracking.
Ran api-server tests in batches, chased specific failures (930,933), then aggregated pass/fail counts with awk (981-983) — per-binary quantified accounting mid-task.
Explicitly re-ran common+api-server after editing the shared `common` crate to confirm no regression — regression-watching on the deep-dependency crate, the anchor-8 behavior.

Final workspace-wide accounting: full suite run, sum passed/failed, count result lines vs test files per crate, confirm exit code, and 'distinguish real failures from test-name matches / check for hidden failures' — careful reconciliation of the 1,390-test picture.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit, repeatedly-updated todo ledger tied to crate milestones, ran per-crate and workspace suites throughout, aggregated pass/fail counts, and deliberately re-ran downstream suites after editing the shared `common` crate to catch regressions — matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because there is no evidence of per-run quantified deltas or explicit thrashing/circular-debugging detection; the most rigorous quantification is concentrated in the final reconciliation. Confidence is medium because the trajectory exposes only action descriptions, not observation output.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Replicaset test failure led to discovering objects must receive uid/resourceVersion on create; the agent revised this storage semantic across memory.rs, lib.rs, AND etcd.rs, then re-ran the failing tests — propagating a corrected contract fact to all affected backends rather than patching one site (matches the '8' anchor).

Sustained recompile→diagnose→fix loop for api-server where falsified assumptions about shared types (ResourceRequirements.claims, autoscaling/HPA types, Service enum fields, Event, CSI) were consistently corrected in the central common crate definitions rather than at call sites — revising the contract, not the symptom.

Scheduler test failure prompted adding Affinity/NodeSelector to shared pod.rs, rebuild, re-run, and an explicit regression check that api-server still passed after the shared-type change — course-correction plus guarding dependents.

volume.rs and core.rs were re-edited many times as new required fields were discovered piecemeal; corrections were reactive/compile-driven rather than a proactive re-derivation and clean refactor, indicating notable churn that keeps it below the '10' anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent never repeats a failing approach or patches only symptoms (excludes 0-3), and it consistently treats compile/test failures as signal to revise the load-bearing shared contract — most clearly by propagating the on-create metadata semantic across both storage backends and by fixing common-crate type definitions rather than call sites, which is squarely the '8' description. It falls short of 10 because corrections are reactive rather than proactively re-derived from the reference, and there is meaningful churn (volume.rs/core.rs re-edited repeatedly) rather than a clean up-front refactor. Landing at 7: solidly propagating corrected contract facts with a mild churn penalty.

rubric.task_read: A massive long-horizon build: reimplement ten interdependent Rust crates that reconstruct Kubernetes (API types, storage, Axum API server, scheduler, controllers, kubelet, proxy, kubectl, cloud, all-in-one) against a fixed public API, 1,390 provided tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite that punishes fixture-fitting without real K8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, a load-bearing contract that cannot be changed, deep cross-crate dependencies, and a mounted v1.35 upstream reference that is the source of truth. This task demands heavy, sustained, well-sequenced meta-work: a skilled practitioner would mine the reference and stubs hard, build leaf-to-root, verify per-crate against real semantics, and constantly track which of 100 binaries pass.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference mining
dimensions.description: Reconstructing the load-bearing public API from tests/stubs/manifests and mining the mounted upstream v1.35 reference for behavior, rather than coding from memory.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key format) is fixed and untestable to guess; the hidden conformance suite requires genuine K8s semantics available only from /opt/k8s-reference. Acting blind here guarantees compile failures and semantic misses.

anchors.0: Starts editing crates without reading tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, or the reference tree; invents APIs from memory.
anchors.3: Skims a few test files and a stub; consults the reference occasionally but mostly codes from general K8s recollection.
anchors.5: Reads the tests and stubs for the crate at hand and derives its expected signatures/field names; consults the reference for the specific component being built.
anchors.8: Systematically extracts the contract per crate (types, module paths, serde field names, storage-key shape) from tests and cross-checks each against the upstream reference; probes the dependency graph before committing to an order; notes semantics the hidden suite will likely exercise.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven orientation across the whole workspace: maps the full crate contract and cross-crate invariants up front, repeatedly returns to the reference to resolve exact behavior (watches, status subresources, controller reconciliation) rather than approximating, and records discovered contract facts so later crates reuse them instead of re-deriving.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered dependency-respecting sequence of sub-goals, each with a concrete done-check (e.g. a crate's provided tests pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The crates form a dependency DAG; the spec itself prescribes leaf-first (common → storage → api-server → upward). Wrong ordering means churning on higher crates whose foundations shift underneath, wasting enormous effort over a long horizon.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated crates or tries to make everything compile at once with no ordering rationale.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates' with no dependency ordering or per-crate completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-to-root order with per-crate build/test as the milestone for each.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware plan with milestones tied to concrete checks (workspace builds, then per-crate provided-test green), sequencing sub-modules within large crates and deferring dependents until their foundation is verified.
anchors.10: A living, granular milestone hierarchy that respects the true dependency DAG, decomposes the hardest crates (api-server, scheduler, kubelet) into internally ordered checkpoints each with an explicit exit test, and is re-sequenced as dependencies are discovered — sustaining coherent forward motion across all 100 test binaries.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond provided fixtures
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided tests AND designing checks for real K8s semantics the hidden conformance suite will test, rather than assuming green fixtures means done.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns that passing visible fixtures without correct Kubernetes semantics fails the hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count toward score. The agent must verify behavior (camelCase JSON, storage keys, watches, status subresources) against the reference, not just the visible suite.

anchors.0: No verification loop; writes code and assumes it works, or never runs the test suite.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test sporadically; treats compile success or a subset of passing tests as done.
anchors.5: Runs the prescribed per-crate and workspace test commands and iterates until provided tests pass.
anchors.8: Systematically drives each crate's provided tests to green, then validates end-to-end semantics (boots the all-in-one binary, checks HTTP behavior/JSON shape/storage keys against the reference) anticipating the hidden conformance suite; distinguishes counted vs non-counted checks.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: per-crate provided tests, workspace-wide runs, plus self-authored semantic probes (used as diagnostics, not for score) that mirror likely conformance assertions and are cross-checked against upstream behavior — catching semantic gaps that visible fixtures miss and confirming they're fixed before moving on.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across 100 binaries
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, current picture of which crates build, which of the 1,390 tests pass, and where effort is stuck, across a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Success requires every non-skipped provided test to pass; with 100 binaries and deep dependencies, losing track means undetected regressions and circular debugging. An accurate done-vs-remaining ledger is what sustains progress.

anchors.0: No awareness of overall state; can't say what passes or what's left; repeats fixed work or misses regressions.
anchors.3: Occasional ad hoc test runs with no consolidated view of remaining failures.
anchors.5: Periodically runs the suite and works down a list of failing crates/tests, roughly tracking remaining work.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of build status and per-binary pass counts, watches for regressions when editing shared crates, and detects when a debugging effort is going in circles.
anchors.10: Continuous, precise progress accounting across the whole workspace: quantified pass/fail deltas per run, early detection of thrashing or a crate that keeps re-breaking downstream tests, and deliberate reprioritization based on that signal — never loses the plot across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising approach when a contract assumption, chosen implementation, or ordering turns out wrong — rather than forcing a falsified design forward.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reconstructing a fixed contract from indirect evidence means assumptions will be wrong (a signature, a serialization detail, an ordering); a large workspace punishes barrelling ahead on a bad assumption. Recognizing and reversing course cheaply is decisive over this horizon.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach without change; ignores contradicting test/compile evidence.
anchors.3: Makes local patches to symptoms but doesn't revise the underlying wrong assumption.
anchors.5: When tests or the compiler reveal a wrong assumption, backs out and adopts a corrected approach for that crate.
anchors.8: Treats compile/test failures and reference discrepancies as signal to revise the design or sequencing, propagating a corrected contract fact to all affected crates rather than patching one call site.
anchors.10: Proactively updates the plan and shared abstractions when reality diverges — recognizes a foundational misunderstanding (e.g. a storage or watch semantic) early, re-derives it from the reference, and cleanly refactors dependents, avoiding both stubborn persistence and needless churn.
